feedback.problem: Given that $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}+{y}^{2}),$ find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ exists.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y)$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}+{y}^{2} & >0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{3}+{y}^{2}>0}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}+{y}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}+{y}^{2} & \ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{x}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{x}}={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{3}+{y}^{2}\ne 0}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{x}} & ={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{3}+{y}^{2}>0}\cap {(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{3}+{y}^{2}\ne 0} \\  & ={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{3}+{y}^{2}>0}.\end{aligned}
$$
